added.author: QCP Capital
added.title: Midterm event vol priced at 47 as downside skew stays bid
added.view: QCP said the midterm event was priced at 47 vol and option flows were light. Some traders sold the 6 Nov 82k/85k call spread to fade upside. Downside skew stayed bid, which QCP linked mainly to the Binance hack. That news also drew two 1,000 BTC blocks of mid-November $74k puts.

added.author: Glassnode
added.title: Skew breaks above its high band as traders pay for protection
added.view: Glassnode's week 45 Market Pulse reports that the BTC 25-delta skew moved above its high band. Implied volatility jumped with the drop, leaving the volatility spread well above its high band. Options open interest contracted after Friday's monthly expiry.

added.author: Greeks.live
added.title: Post-election IV stabilises; little year-end move priced
added.view: Greeks.live said implied volatility across major maturities rose about 1 point after the midterms, and the election-driven IV spike has largely stabilised. In its view, the options market does not expect any significant BTC move by year-end.

added.author: Deribit
added.title: $2.86B expiry: BTC call-weighted, ETH tilted to puts
added.view: Deribit reported about $2.86B in BTC and ETH options expiring 6 Nov. BTC was $2.64B notional with a 0.38 put/call ratio, a $79K max pain and call concentrations at $82K and $85K. ETH was $224.5M with a 1.27 put/call ratio and a $2.35K max pain.

added.author: Block Scholes
added.title: BTC implied vol eases while SOL climbs
added.view: Block Scholes' BSIV puts 30-day implied volatility at 41.9% for BTC (down 1.4 points over 7 days), 60.7% for ETH (up 0.5) and 67.1% for SOL (up 4.1). This came as US equities had their worst day since April 2025.

added.author: Block Scholes
added.title: BTC options turnover hits a one-month high on election day
added.view: Across Deribit, Bybit and OKX, daily BTC options turnover peaked at $6.8B on 4 Nov, the heaviest session in a month. Calls were 54% of BTC volume, and 55–56% for ETH, SOL and HYPE. HYPE turnover peaked at $42M, down from $132M the week before.
